api-foundations.copy: Segmented Control API exposes items, selectedKey, variant, state, density, and ariaLabel while Design System owns focus, spacing, and state precedence.

props.name: items
props.type: Array<{ key?: string; value?: string; label: string; icon?: string }>
props.notes: Visible segments with stable keys and optional icons.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Presentation variant for the local segmented surface.

props.name: density
props.notes: Maps segment target sizing to Density.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for one local mutually exclusive choice.
Keep labels visible even when icons are present.
Keep the selected item announced with aria-selected.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use for page navigation.
Do not combine unrelated controls inside the group.
Do not use it as a dashboard filter bar.

groups.title: Review
items: Check mobile wrapping and label fit.
Check selected/current uses Flow action-primary with enough contrast.
Check the control remains visually distinct from Tabs.

mustTest: Outlined, toolbar, compact, and icon-only variants render distinct geometry
rejectIf: Toolbar or compact is only documented but not implemented in package styles.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Segmented Control as one local exclusive choice. Agents may place it for view mode or density mode, while humans confirm whether the request is actually navigation, tabs, or a filter pattern.
canDecide: Use Segmented Control for view mode, chart mode, local layout density, or map/list switch.
Keep each segment as a single option with visible text.
Use warning only when the current mode has a policy or availability caveat.
mustAsk: The control changes page route, saved view, or dashboard query.
The group needs more than one selected value.
Labels cannot fit in the available viewport.
miel.handoff: I am using Segmented Control for one local exclusive mode. Please confirm labels, selected key, keyboard movement, responsive wrapping, and that this is not navigation or a filter bar.
